title: "Financial and Price-Basis Assumptions"
completion: 40

## Role in the Model

This page defines the common monetary basis, lifecycle capital basis and annual
cost calculation. Component pages retain ownership of source values,
component-specific scaling, installation boundaries, replacement scope and
annual OPEX.

## Canonical Monetary Basis

All costs entering a common model result are expressed in **constant 2025 euros
(EUR~2025~)**. Each imported cost retains its source currency, source price
year and cost boundary.

A value with an unresolved price year cannot be adopted as an EUR~2025~ model
input. It may be shown only as a non-combinable reference until the evidence
gap is resolved.

No generic geographic, offshore or market multiplier is applied. Such a factor
may be introduced only where evidence defines its scope and prevents overlap
with component, installation or commercial allowances.

The [BOP reference](../hydrogen_production/balance_of_plant.qmd) uses an explicit
screening exception: the undated DNV water-treatment indication is assumed to
be EUR2023 and escalated using euro-area HICP. This assumption does not establish
the supplier quote year or change the rule for other costs.

## Currency and Price-Year Normalization

A source cost in currency $s$ and price year $y$ is normalized as:

$$
C_{2025,\mathrm{EUR}}
=
C_{y,s}
\frac{I_{s,k}(2025)}{I_{s,k}(y)}
FX_{\mathrm{EUR}/s,2025}
G_{\mathrm{market}}.
$$

| Symbol | Definition | Unit or status |
|---|---|---|
| $C_{y,s}$ | Source cost in source currency $s$ and price year $y$ | currency $s$ |
| $I_{s,k}(t)$ | Price index for cost type $k$ in source market $s$ | index |
| $FX_{\mathrm{EUR}/s,2025}$ | 2025 annual-average euros per unit of source currency | EUR/currency $s$ |
| $G_{\mathrm{market}}$ | Separately evidenced geographic-market adjustment | dimensionless; default 1.0 |
| $C_{2025,\mathrm{EUR}}$ | Cost on the common model basis | EUR~2025~ |

Escalation is performed in the source currency before currency conversion. A
cost-specific index is preferred where its scope matches the equipment or
activity. A consumer-price index may be used only as a transparent fallback,
with the mismatch recorded as a limitation.

US-dollar escalation to 2025 uses the U.S. CPI-U annual averages as the
documented consumer-price fallback, because no single cost-specific index
covers the mixed equipment scopes involved [@blsCpiU2026]. The annual averages
are {{< var financial-usd-cpi-2020-value >}} (2020), {{< var financial-usd-cpi-2022-value >}} (2022) and {{< var financial-usd-cpi-2025-value >}} (2025; eleven months, as BLS
published no October 2025 value), giving
`financial-usd-escalation-2020-2025` = {{< var financial-usd-escalation-2020-2025 >}}
and `financial-usd-escalation-2022-2025` = {{< var financial-usd-escalation-2022-2025 >}}.
A component that has a better-matched index, such as the compressor producer
price index, uses its own factor instead.

For USD-to-EUR conversions, the common convention is the ECB 2025 annual
average of 1 EUR = {{< var financial-usd-per-eur-2025-value >}} USD. The inverse
rate is {{< var financial-eur-per-usd-2025 >}}
[@ecb2025USDEUR]. A dated exchange rate is not mixed with annual-average price
indices in an EUR~2025~ model input.

The [platform benchmark comparison](../platforms/platform_material_capex.qmd)
uses a documented screening exception: source-year average FX followed by
euro-area HICP escalation. Its adopted central coefficient is a EUR~2023~
modelling judgement escalated to EUR~2025~. This does not establish a
sector-specific construction index or change other components' normalisation.

## Project Financial Assumptions

| Parameter | Symbol | Value | Classification and basis |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Real weighted average cost of capital | $r$ | {{< var financial-real-wacc >}} | Provisional project-wide modelling assumption; evidence basis and sensitivity remain unresolved |
| Project life | $n$ | {{< var financial-project-life >}} | Project-wide modelling assumption |
| Residual value | — | {{< var financial-residual-value-fraction >}} | Modelling convention at the project-life endpoint |
| Decommissioning allowance | — | {{< var financial-decommissioning-fraction >}} of total offshore installation CAPEX | Simplified modelling assumption |

The same {{< var financial-real-wacc >}} real WACC applies to all three architectures. Tax, debt,
construction-finance timing and architecture-specific financing are not
modelled.

## Capital Recovery Factor

$$
CRF
=
\frac{r(1+r)^n}{(1+r)^n-1}.
$$

For a real WACC of {{< var financial-real-wacc >}} and a project life of
{{< var financial-project-life >}}, the resulting capital recovery factor is
{{< var financial-capital-recovery-factor >}}.

## Component Replacement

Replacement is included only when a component owner documents:

1. a material technical life shorter than {{< var financial-project-life >}};
2. the replaced scope;
3. the replacement cost; and
4. that continued operation requires the replacement.

For such a component:

$$
N_{\mathrm{replacement},j}
=
\left\lceil
\frac{n}{n_j}
\right\rceil-1.
$$

A replacement at the end of the {{< var financial-project-life >}} project life is not counted. Components with a
technical life of at least {{< var financial-project-life >}} have zero replacement. A short nominal life
does not create a replacement cost unless the component page defines the event
and boundary.

Total replacement cost is:

$$
C_{\mathrm{replacement}}
=
\sum_j
N_{\mathrm{replacement},j}
C_{\mathrm{replacement},j}.
$$

Replacement timing is not discounted under the approved screening convention.

## Decommissioning

The model uses an installation-cost proxy for separately costed installation and an explicit removal-cost input for the combined platform EPCI package:

$$
C_{\mathrm{decommissioning}}
=
f_{\mathrm{decommissioning}}
C_{\mathrm{separate\ offshore\ installation}}
+ C_{\mathrm{platform\ decommissioning}}.
$$

The separate offshore-installation total contains non-overlapping installation costs
from the installation pages, excluding platform installation already bundled in EPCI.
$C_{\mathrm{platform\ decommissioning}}$ is the `platform-decommissioning-cost`
input in EUR~2025~. It is initially unresolved, not zero. Missing platform
decommissioning blocks complete lifetime cost and LCOH but does not block platform
CAPEX. The installation-cost fraction is never applied to the whole EPCI package.
For architectures without a central platform, no platform removal term is added. The factor $f_{\mathrm{decommissioning}}$ is
{{< var financial-decommissioning-fraction >}} and is an explicit modelling assumption,
not a sourced contractor estimate. Decommissioning timing is not discounted.

## Lifecycle Capital Basis and Annual Cost

$$
C_{\mathrm{lifecycle\ capital}}
=
C_{\mathrm{initial}}
+
C_{\mathrm{replacement}}
+
C_{\mathrm{decommissioning}}.
$$

$$
C_{\mathrm{annual}}
=
CRF
C_{\mathrm{lifecycle\ capital}}
+
\sum_j O_j.
$$

Every $O_j$ is an annual, non-overlapping component OPEX term in
EUR~2025~/year.

Development, shared owner engineering, insurance and owner contingency are
**outside the model scope** (agreed decision). Results are reported as
technical-scope costs and are labelled accordingly; they are not total project
costs.

## Manufactured-Cost Markup

The {{< var hydrogen-manufactured-cost-markup >}} factor used for selected NREL PEM stack, balance-of-plant and
power-electronics inputs is not a general financial escalation factor:

$$
C_{\mathrm{purchased}}
=
k_{\mathrm{markup}}C_{\mathrm{manufactured}}.
$$

The factor $k_{\mathrm{markup}}$ is {{< var hydrogen-manufactured-cost-markup >}}
and is an explicit component-level modelling assumption. Badgett et
al. document the manufactured-cost boundary but do not provide or validate the
markup [@badgett2024PEMCost]. The component owner must prevent the markup from
being applied to procurement or installed-system prices and must keep
installation, offshore packaging, soft costs and inflation separate.

## Required Checks Before Aggregation

Before costs are added:

1. source currency, price year and scope are known;
2. adopted values are normalized to EUR~2025~;
3. component, installation and project boundaries do not overlap;
4. required unresolved fields return not parameterized;
5. replacement is counted only under the documented rule;
6. decommissioning is applied once to total offshore installation CAPEX; and
7. annual OPEX is not embedded in CAPEX or another component term.

## Implemented conversion routes and provisional O&M

| Cost owner | Implemented conversion to EUR~2025~ |
|---|---|
| Turbine, transformer and foundation | USD2022 CPI-U ratio to 2025, then 2025 USD/EUR |
| PEM stack and NREL BOP reference | USD2020 CPI-U ratio to 2025, then 2025 USD/EUR |
| ORBIT installation rates | USD2024 CPI-U ratio to 2025, then 2025 USD/EUR |
| BVG turbine installation | GBP2024 UK CPI ratio to 2025, then 2025 GBP/EUR |
| Compressor | CAD source converted using the documented source FX, compressor-specific US PPI escalation, then 2025 USD/EUR; see [Compressor](../hydrogen_infra/compressor.qmd) |
| DNV thermal water-treatment allowance | Explicit EUR2023 assumption followed by HICP |
| Platform benchmark observations | Source-year FX followed by HICP; central EPCI coefficient starts in EUR2023 |
| Confidential pipeline fit | Owner-confirmed EUR2025/m; conversion factor is unity |

The CPI-U factors are derived from canonical index inputs in code, rounded to
five decimal places to preserve the established cost results. They are no longer
independently entered scalar factors. Component-specific exceptions retain their
own evidence; no generic index replaces them.

For lifecycle calculations, the user-selected provisional allowance is:

$$
C_{\mathrm{O\&M},i}=f_{\mathrm{O\&M}}\left(C_{\mathrm{supply},i}
+C_{\mathrm{installation},i}+C_{\mathrm{EPCI},i}\right).
$$

Here $C_{\mathrm{O\&M},i}$ is annual O&M in EUR~2025~/year and
$f_{\mathrm{O\&M}}$ is {{< var financial-provisional-opex-rate >}}, an explicit
user assumption selected on 15 October 2026. Capital entries are mutually
exclusive where EPCI already includes supply and installation. This is a
percentage of initial, non-annualised CAPEX; it replaces the earlier component
rates. A missing included capital cost blocks that component's complete O&M.
Detailed activity-based O&M is deferred. The article's production/CAPEX reporting
scope continues to defer O&M and other lifecycle results.

Residual value is fixed at zero, including at the project endpoint. Nonzero
scenario overrides are rejected. The decommissioning proxy includes offshore
installation entries only; onshore hydrogen-receipt installation is excluded.
The explicit platform removal cost remains a separate term, since platform
installation is already bundled into EPCI. The article excludes onshore receipt
costs as a boundary assumption; delivery pressure does not establish zero
physical connection cost.
